thread:
maya: FYI bringing up the converted HF->Redwood q4 model, seeing streaming cutoffs where the client gets [DONE] early.
ryan: repro steps?
maya: steps below, small prompt. conversion used hf-to-redwood tool + bitsandbytes 4-bit quant. streaming returns truncated output, sometimes stops mid-sentence.
maya: repro snippet:
```
# convert
python tools/convert.py --model-orig /mnt/models/gptx --out /redwood/models/gptx-q4 --quantize q4_0
# start serving via local dev instance
REDWOOD_ENV=dev ./bin/redwood serve --model /redwood/models/gptx-q4 --port 8080
# curl streaming endpoint
curl -N -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/stream -d '{"input":"Write a short paragraph about Redwood inference and productionizing LLMs."}'
```
maya: logs show repeated eos tokens in decode path:
```
[decoder] token emitted: 50256
[decoder] token emitted: 50256
[stream] sent [DONE]
```
maya: token 50256 is `` from HF tokenizer but our chat template also injects "</s>" as EOS.
devx: do we have additional_special_tokens in tokenizer.json? that can create duplicate eos mapping.
maya: tokenizer.json contains: "bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>", "additional_special_tokens": [""] , plus chat template postprocess appends "</s>" again.
ryan: aha. so the conversion left both as valid EOSs. runtime sees first eos byte sequence, flushes stream and then emits second eos which triggers [DONE] earlier because we treat any eos as final.
kai: quick mitigation: map all known eos variants to a single EOS id during conversion. e.g. in convert.py add a pass that merges additional_special_tokens matching empty string to eos_id.
kai: patch suggestion:
```
# pseudo
if tokenizer.additional_special_tokens contains "":
    tokenizer.add_special_tokens({"eos_token": ""})
    tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids("</s>") -> id of ""
```
ryan: also check chat template insertion: some templates include both end markers to delimit system/user turns which now collide.
devx: would adding an explicit stop sequence in serving request help? like stop=["\n\n"] to avoid relying on EOS semantics.
maya: yes that's a useful stopgap for apps, but underlying ambiguity will still cause flaky streaming metrics and regen costs.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: new model gptx-q4 failed canary on staging at 2026-03-19T12:07Z (reason: streaming early termination) :warning:
kai: long-term we should canonicalize EOS tokens in conversion, add a conversion-time validator that emits a warning if multiple tokens map to eos. unit test for streaming should include case where tokenizer has two eos tokens.
ryan: also saw this only after quantization — maybe quant path uses a different token id mapping step that preserves both tokens. need to compare original hf tokenizer.ids_to_tokens vs converted.ids_to_tokens.
maya: I'll open a small PR with the conversion fix + repro test. in meantime, app teams can set explicit stop sequences or disable auto-eos streaming flush.
maya: thanks, will ping when PR is up :thumbsup:
